claim: The assembly and maintenance of all cilia and flagella require intraflagellar transport (IFT) along the axoneme.

evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established fact in the field of ciliary biology, drawing from established scientific consensus and supported by the citation context of the manuscript.

claim: IFT trains are coupled to flagellar membrane glycoproteins (FMGs) in a Ca2+-dependent manner.

evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically the calcium manipulation experiments shown in Figure 5.

evidence_reasoning: This is supported by direct experimental observations shown in Figures 1 and 2, where IFT train pausing was visualized during gliding motility.

claim: Each IFT train is transported by at least four motors.
